acts.label: Prologue
acts.desc: Host Ira Glass talks about our fascination with small things.

acts.label: Act One
acts.desc: An endocrinologist wrote the show about a wave of parents coming to her to treat their short (but otherwise healthy) children with human growth hormone. Contributor Scott Brown investigates.
acts.title: Coming Up Short

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc: David Kestenbaum talks about his love of the number zero and its power to destroy. Among zero's victims: one of the most controversial laws in recent memory.
acts.title: Let’s Give ‘Em Nothing to Talk About

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Lilly Sullivan tells the story of the writer Robert Walser, who moved into a mental hospital and then seemed to disappear from the world. Until people looked more closely. To read more about Robert Walser, including some of the writings talked about in this story, read Microscripts, a book translated by Susan Bernofsky.
acts.title: What the Eye Can’t See
